definition: Audio mining is a technique by which the content of an audio signal can be automatically analyzed and searched.
details: It is most commonly used in the field of automatic speech recognition, where the analysis tries to identify any speech within the audio. The term audio mining is sometimes used interchangeably with audio indexing, phonetic searching, phonetic indexing, speech indexing, audio analytics, speech analytics, word spotting, and information retrieval. Audio indexing, however, is mostly used to describe the pre-process of audio mining, in which the audio file is broken down into a searchable index of words.

explainer.lead: Audio mining makes the contents of recordings searchable instead of leaving them locked inside sound files. It is especially useful when large collections of speech would be impractical to review by listening from start to finish.

tiers.eli5: Imagine turning a pile of voice recordings into a book with an index at the back. Instead of listening to every recording, you could search for a word and find where it was spoken. Audio mining is the process that makes this possible.
tiers.practitioner: Audio mining is commonly applied through automatic speech recognition to locate and analyze speech in audio. A typical workflow builds a searchable word index during audio indexing, then uses that index for searching or retrieval. Keep indexing—the preprocessing stage—distinct from the broader mining and analysis workflow.
tiers.paperLevel: Given an audio signal A, audio mining automatically derives a representation R(A) whose content can be analyzed and searched, commonly by identifying speech within A. Audio indexing is the preprocessing step that decomposes the audio into a searchable word index. Terminology varies: audio mining is sometimes used interchangeably with phonetic searching, speech indexing, speech analytics, word spotting, and information retrieval.

explainer.example: A researcher has a collection of recorded interviews and wants every mention of “climate.” Audio mining identifies the speech and builds a word index, allowing the researcher to search for that term instead of replaying every interview.

usedIn.name: Automatic speech recognition
usedIn.detail: Identifies speech within audio so its content can be analyzed and searched.

usedIn.name: Information retrieval
usedIn.detail: Supports searches over spoken content rather than requiring manual listening.

usedIn.name: Speech analytics
usedIn.detail: Analyzes speech content through a closely related use of audio-mining terminology.

explainer.intuition: Listening is sequential, but search is direct: audio mining turns spoken content into something a search system can examine. Its central task is usually to find and represent speech so words in a recording can be located.
howItWorks: Take an audio signal as input.
Analyze the signal to identify any speech it contains.
Break the audio into a searchable index of words.
Search or analyze that index to locate spoken content.
explainer.whyItMatters: It makes spoken information accessible to automatic search and analysis. This removes the need to treat every recording as an opaque file that can only be understood through manual listening.
misconceptions: Audio indexing is not quite the whole process: it usually refers to preprocessing audio into a searchable word index.
Audio mining is not limited to playing or classifying sounds; its defining purpose is automatic analysis and search of audio content.
Its terminology is not fully standardized, so names such as speech indexing and speech analytics may be used interchangeably with it.
